diagnosis: The first prospective unchanged replication reproduced the original CPU RSS failure to within 905216 bytes: 812425216 versus 813330432. The measurement is therefore reproducible. The serving process reconstructs and validates the 254 MB signed core archive before activating the same archive; that one-time packaging path allocates full state, safe-tensor payload, archive, and verification buffers in the serving process before runtime activation. Garbage collection does not guarantee that those allocator arenas are returned to the operating system. The product lifecycle must materialize the immutable archive before the serving process and activate the content-addressed archive directly.
decision: Stop r2 and r3 exactly as preregistered. Implement one bounded activation-lifecycle repair: materialize and authenticate the exact existing core archive outside the serving process, bind its archive and payload hashes, then load that unchanged artifact directly in fresh CPU and CUDA product screens. Preserve every quality, speed, TTFT, active-memory, RSS, sparse-execution, identity, and output threshold.
claim_boundary: Reproducible CPU memory failure and authorization for one exact-artifact lifecycle repair only. This is not a Phase 7 pass and does not authorize model, package, prompt, or threshold changes.
